newsitem.title: PERU: Rescuers battle to reach snowstorm victims in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers battle to reach snowstorm victims in Peru.

text.p: Rescue workers battled through a wall of snow on Monday to get medicine and aid to hundreds of people trapped on a mountain highway in the Peruvian Andes by a snowstorm that has already claimed six lives.

An army helicopter airlifted two elderly people suffering from breathing problems who were caught on the snow-covered road, 11,650 feet (3,500 metres) above sea level. They were taken to nearby Abancay, 380 miles (610 km) southeast of Lima, Civil Defence official Luis Barra told Reuters.
Soldiers, who walked to the snowbound area on Sunday, found the bodies of six people, including three infants, who froze to death inside their trapped vehicles.
The storm, which started on Friday, originally stranded about a thousand people in 40 vehicles, including 12 passenger buses, on a 50-mile (80-km) stretch of road.

But as the weather improved on Monday, some drivers ploughed through up to 5-foot (1.5-metre) of snow to reach safety. An estimated 30 vehicles and 800 people were still stuck on the road at mid-afternoon, Civil Defence officials said.
Most of those still on the mountainside were in stable condition and received aid from rescue workers, who arrived by road in wide-traction vehicles, Barra said.

The army postponed more airlifts to fly out survivors later on Monday because the storm had gained strength again. Forecasters predicted it would subside by the end of the day and with snowplows clearing the road, more vehicles were expected to reach safety later on Monday or Tuesday.
Weather changes caused by the El Nino current warming surface waters in the Pacific Ocean have resulted in unusually cold temperatures this year in the Andes Mountain range.
The unusually strong storm affected the areas of Ayacucho, Apurimac and Arequipa, covering most highland roads with snow and making driving difficult in many areas.
